Consider the remedy below before continuing; the diagnosis prints the hand-run recipe, but the one-command remedy is `plan-tool convergence telemetry-producer-hardening --apply-split` (in-place re-split) or `plan-tool convergence telemetry-producer-hardening --apply-scope-out` (carve the step out), behind the same apply-or-recommend gate.

## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps, addressed before the completeness gaps below. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks them first, before the completeness gaps. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply telemetry-producer-hardening   # walk + apply each correctness gap, then the completeness gaps
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk telemetry-producer-hardening  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[rejected-restored-edits]`: Serial `apply_finding` records `APPLIED` before `plan_tool/cli/review_actions.py:_dispatch_apply_finding` asks whether to keep the edit, while the plan-level Acceptance criteria require that “rejected/restored edits cannot emit a misleading `APPLIED` verdict.” Step 4 (`Record parallel apply results once from the canonical replay`) suppresses only canonical parse-gate restorations, and step 5 (`Cover apply telemetry forwarding and best-effort guards`) explicitly preserves launcher-side serial recording, so a user-rejected serial edit still resolves as `acted-on`.
- MEDIUM `[empty-applied-diff]`: Step 4 (`Record parallel apply results once from the canonical replay`) says “A selected `APPLIED` … response emits that verdict once,” even when the result has no changes; `plan_tool/telemetry_analysis.py:resolve_decision_inline` maps that token to `acted-on`, while `plan_tool/cli/review_actions.py:_dispatch_apply_finding` treats “APPLIED with empty diff” as a no-op. Canonical parallel telemetry can therefore report an acted-on finding when no edit landed.
- MEDIUM `[step1-append-extraction]`: Step 1 (`Replace oversized code fingerprint maps with a stable digest`) mixes the behavior-preserving instruction to “Move the low-level append into a stdlib-only helper” with new digest persistence and short-write rollback behavior in the same code step.
- HIGH `[snapshot-restoration-failure]`: Step 3 (`Record unusable apply backend responses`) requires a raised invocation to “restore every tracked plan/detail file” and “propagate the original exception unchanged,” but `plan_tool/launcher.py:_restore_text_files` can itself raise while unlinking or writing. The detail never defines which failure takes precedence or how callers avoid continuing with partially restored state, so both guarantees cannot hold unconditionally.
- HIGH `[follow-up-invocation-outcomes]`: Step 3 (`Record unusable apply backend responses`) deliberately says “Auto-fix follow-up invocation outcomes … remain in the run log unless a later plan adds an attempt identity,” while the Problem statement says `apply_finding` “leaves backend invocation failures only in the run log” and plan-level Deferred says “No producer-hardening requirement is deferred.” Retiring #72 in step 6 while the second backend invocation retains the named observability defect contradicts the plan’s closure boundary.
- MEDIUM `[parallel-plan-fingerprint]`: Step 4 (`Record parallel apply results once from the canonical replay`) says a conflict causes “the finding [to be] re-run serially against the now-current canonical tree,” but its `Hoist the fingerprint once` rule says “Reuse it for every replayed event, including conflict reruns” so every event describes “the same pre-dispatch plan state.” A conflict rerun inspects a plan changed by earlier replayed findings, so attaching the pre-dispatch fingerprint makes its selected verdict join to code it did not evaluate.

## Conceptual completeness — reported, not auto-applied

Coverage gaps in the plan's own ideas (orphaned concepts, uncovered risks, dangling criteria, missing edge cases). Each is a scoping judgment call, so the audit's iterate loop does **not** touch them — chasing every newly-surfaced gap would never converge. Walk and apply them with the paired subcommand:

    plan-tool completeness-apply <plan>                # interactive walk over every gap
    plan-tool completeness-apply <plan> --anchor <slug> # address one gap by its `[slug]`

Each finding below carries the exact `--anchor` value plus the command pre-filled — copy-paste to address it.

- HIGH `[snapshot-restoration-failure]`: Step 3 (`Record unusable apply backend responses`) promises to “restore every tracked plan/detail file” and propagate “the original exception unchanged,” but it never defines restoration-failure precedence; HEAD’s `plan_tool/launcher.py:_restore_text_files` can raise from `unlink` or `write_text`, stop partway through the snapshot, and mask the backend exception. The tests cover successful restoration and recorder failure, not a partial or raising restoration.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply telemetry-producer-hardening --anchor snapshot-restoration-failure`
- MEDIUM `[benchmark-apply-ownership]`: Step 5 (`Cover apply telemetry forwarding and best-effort guards`) calls four sites “the four serial apply callers,” but HEAD also calls `apply_finding` from `plan_tool/bench.py:_run_apply`. That caller writes under a per-trial scratch repository which `plan_tool/bench.py:_run_cell_trial` normally deletes, so its apply and `INVOCATION-FAILED` events remain disposable and never reach canonical telemetry; no step defines whether benchmark telemetry should be suppressed or durably owned elsewhere.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply telemetry-producer-hardening --anchor benchmark-apply-ownership`
- HIGH `[follow-up-invocation-outcomes]`: Step 3 (`Record unusable apply backend responses`) limits the new signal to the “primary” invocation and explicitly defers “Auto-fix follow-up invocation outcomes,” saying they “remain in the run log,” while the Problem statement says `apply_finding` backend invocation failures are missing from decision telemetry and `## Deferred` says no producer-hardening requirement remains. A failed or partially mutating follow-up therefore remains invisible in the decision log even though the plan retires all of #72’s producer residual.
  - Address: `plan-tool completeness-apply telemetry-producer-hardening --anchor follow-up-invocation-outcomes`
